etymologies.etymologyHTML: Originally from baby talk. Possibly influenced by Middle English mome (“mother, aunt”), from Old English *mōme, from Proto-West Germanic *mōmā, from Proto-Germanic *mōmǭ (“mother, aunt”), from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂-méh₂, reduplication of *méh₂- (“mother”), related to German Muhme (“aunt”), Latin mamma (“mother, nurse”), Irish mam (“mother”), Lithuanian mama, moma (“mother”).

definitions.definition: (hypocoristic, usually childish, Canada, US) Mother, female parent.

quote.citation: 1990, Prince (lyrics and music), “Nothing Compares 2 U”, performed by Sinéad O’Connor:
quote.text: All the flowers that you planted, mama, in the backyard / All died when you went away
